subject.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write

question: Should config-write callers receive this comment-loss diagnostic through the new exported `warning?: string` fields, or should the warning remain output-only or use a generalized diagnostics contract?
rationale: The patch is behaviorally sound, but selecting a permanent exported result shape is API design that automation should not decide from tests alone.

options.title: Approve additive warning fields
options.body: Keep the optional warning on both write and mutation results, document it as the machine-readable quiet-mode contract, and remove the dead-code exception before merge.

options.title: Keep logger-only warning
options.body: Remove the result fields and emit only through the existing warning channel, accepting that output-suppressed callers will not receive the diagnostic.

options.title: Generalize diagnostics first
options.body: Replace the singular field with an extensible typed or plural diagnostics shape before establishing the exported contract.

recommendation.title: Approve additive warning fields
recommendation.body: Keep the optional warning on both write and mutation results, document it as the machine-readable quiet-mode contract, and remove the dead-code exception before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of config-write safety and public configuration behavior, making this the strongest available routing candidate for the contract choice.
